shipped_rows.title_o: The Relationship between Sensory Sensitivity and Autistic Traits in the General Population

blind_target.authors: Sapey-Triomphe L-A, Moulin A, Sonié S, Schmitz C
blind_target.title: The Glasgow Sensory Questionnaire: validation of a French language version and refinement of sensory profiles of people with high Autism-Spectrum Quotient
blind_target.evidence_quote: The two main goals of this study were: (a) the validation of the German version of the GSQ according to the Universalist model of cross-cultural adaptation [ 29 ] and (b) the replication of sensory processing differences of individuals with higher or lower AQ scores as reported in the original English version by Robertson and Simmons [ 48 ] and in the French version of Sapey-Triomphe et al. [ 51 ].
blind_target.outcome_quote: Contrary to expectations, only 35 out of 297 students had AQ scores higher than 26 in our sample. Therefore, the present sample seems not suitable for drawing meaningful conclusions about the sensory processing differences of individuals with higher AQ scores.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The authors also call the replication unsuccessful, but explicitly judge their sample unsuitable for meaningful conclusions because too few participants had high AQ. The codebook special verdict for a non-adjudicating attempt takes precedence. Both named targets are included in the replication objective.

prior_decision.quote: Regarding the second aim, it was expected that the German student sample would show similar sensory processing differences as the French sample depending on whether participants scored higher or lower on the AQ [ 51 ]. More precisely, a stronger correlation between hyper- and hyposensitivity, higher hypersensitivity scores in relation to hyposensitivity scores, and a more homogeneous pattern of sensory processing differences in all seven sensory modalities for individuals with higher compared to individuals with lower AQ scores were expected.
prior_decision.reason: This study explicitly re-tests the sensory profile findings reported by Sapey-Triomphe et al. (2018) [51] in addition to Robertson and Simmons (2013) [48], making Sapey-Triomphe et al. (2018) an omitted replication target.

luna_triage.reason: The paper explicitly identifies the French sensory-profile findings by Sapey-Triomphe et al. [51] as a replication aim, and the Results report the outcome of that aim. The sole supplied row 1199 is Robertson and Simmons’s distinct English original; it does not represent the separately cited French study. The reference entry establishes the target identity and DOI.
